close.needRef: roadmap close: a card number is needed, for example kermach roadmap close t12 --done "…" --proof "…". Help — kermach roadmap --help
close.badArg: argument {a} not understood. Help — kermach roadmap --help
close.noFileWhy: --no-file needs a reason: why there is no proof file, for example --no-file "cancelled: done in t12"
close.noFileAgent: roadmap close --no-file: no access — the command was called by a card agent (tab with KERMACH_CARD). Only the main session can close a card without a file; the agent saves the check output to a file and names it in --proof
close.proofAndNoFile: roadmap close: --proof and --no-file cannot be used together: either a file or the reason why there is none
close.needBoth: roadmap close: both are needed — --done "what was done" and --proof "proof file"
close.badTested: roadmap close: --tested: wrong value {bad}. Allowed: {ok}; several — separated by commas. The card is not closed
close.badUsed: roadmap close: --used not understood: {bad} — --used lists only the notes that helped, and how: "helped: d<number> — how it helped", "how" at least two words, several — separated by ";", for example --used "helped: d12 — found the same cause". Do not list notes that did not help; if none helped, close without --used. The card is not closed
close.notOwn: card not closed: no access — this tab works on {own}, but closing {ref} was requested. A card agent closes only its own card; another card is closed by its agent or the main session. If you found that {ref} is already done, record it as a note: kermach roadmap new d "…" --type note
close.needTested: card not closed: --tested is needed, what the work was checked on. Real — what the person will work with: a real agent, window, installer, site or server. Fake — a stand-in agent, stub, test board. Human only — only the person can check it. Several — separated by commas, for example --tested "real, fake". A stand-in check is fine, but it must not be hidden. Help — kermach roadmap --help
close.hintAgent: . There will be no new file (the person did or accepted the work, the card is cancelled) — only the main session can close a card without a file; the card agent sets status: awaiting answer and writes the question into the card
close.hintMain: . There will be no file (the person did the work, the card is cancelled) — close it like this: --no-file "reason"; --no-file is available only to the main session, not to a card agent tab. If the person accepted the work or answered in words, first run kermach roadmap answer {ref} "the person's words", otherwise the reviewer will not see those words and will return the card
close.whyNoFile: --proof names no file that exists on disk. --proof says: "{said}". Searched from folders: {bases}. What to do: save the check output or a screenshot as a file in {dir} and name its path in --proof
close.whyOld: all files from --proof are older than the start of work on the card, {since}: {list}. What to do: run the check again, save its output as a fresh file in {dir} and name it in --proof
close.whyOnlyOld: "How to check" requires an --only run, but only-result.txt is older than the start of work on the card, {since}: {list}. What to do: run --only again, copy the result to only-result.txt and name it in --proof
close.whyNoOnly: "How to check" requires an --only run, but --proof has no only-result.txt file. What to do: run --only, copy the result to {dir}only-result.txt and name this path in --proof
close.whyNotProof: --proof has only files that prove nothing: {list}. Board files, session logs and edited files from the "Files" field are not proof. What to do: save the check output or a screenshot as a file in {dir} and name its path in --proof
close.whyOnlyEmpty: "How to check" requires an --only run, but only-result.txt is empty: {list}. What to do: run --only, copy its result to only-result.txt and name it in --proof
close.listHowNew: What to do: put the file {rel} — one line per item of the fields "What to do" and "How to check": "- item — proof file[:line]", several files — separated by ";", for example "- refusal without a file — {example}". A file is check output, a screenshot or a place in edited code; words without a file are not proof
close.listHowFix: What to do: fix {rel}: one line per item of the fields "What to do" and "How to check": "- item — proof file[:line]", several files — separated by ";", for example "- refusal without a file — {example}". A file is check output, a screenshot or a place in edited code; words without a file are not proof
close.listOld: all files in {rel} are older than the start of work on the card, {since}: the newest is {newest}. What to do: run the check again, save its output anew as a file in {dir} and name it in the list next to the item it proves. Other items may point to old files
close.redNames: checks failed in the --only result: {names} ({files}). A card with a red check is not closed: fix it and run --only again. If the failure is not caused by your work — do not close the card, set status: awaiting answer and ask the person
close.copyStale: unchanged since the copy was created
close.redVerdict: the gate gave no result in the --only output: "{verdict}" ({files}). A card with a red check is not closed: fix it and run --only again. If the failure is not caused by your work — do not close the card, set status: awaiting answer and ask the person
close.redMain: . The person said to close although the check is red — first kermach roadmap answer {ref} "the person's words", then close with --no-file "reason" instead of --proof; --no-file is available only to the main session
close.links: wrong file:line links {where}. What to do: open each link, fix the path (from the project folder; a path with a space — in backticks) or the line number and close again. A link from a quote (someone else's error text, the reviewer's words) or to a deleted file — put the quote in "…" together with the words around it, or write "deleted", "was", "Error:" before the link — such links are not checked
flag.wave: The load flag is set right now ({file} in the project folder): the wave is accepted, but it starts no new cards until the file is removed. What to do: the flag is set when the laptop runs short of memory; remove the file once the load drops, and the wave continues by itself, no new command needed
flag.status: Load flag: set ({file} in the project folder) — waves start no new cards, reviewers wait. Remove the file once the load drops, and everything continues by itself
flag.closeAgent: . The load flag is set right now ({file} in the project folder): do not run anything heavy (--only, an Electron probe, real claude or codex). The check cannot be run — write into the card what was done and the reason "no access: load flag", set status: awaiting answer
flag.closeMain: . The load flag is set right now ({file} in the project folder): --only checks and Electron probes do not run until the file is removed. Remove it once the load drops and run the check again
